engineering_question: Can a fixed positive matrix-polynomial energy majorant tighten the inherited header residual enough to cross the saved necessary gap threshold, without changing the continuous model or evaluating a new response?
limits: Authenticate the saved header free/free block against its existing exact positive certificate. Reuse its eigenvalue lower bound, datum, exact sparse action, original candidate and both correction boxes. U is the exact matrix infinity norm.

Predeclare exactly 64 matrix applications. Evaluate only the scalar polynomial energy upper with exact Fractions and a positive terminal remainder. No adaptive stopping, inverse matrix, factorization, optimized trial or displacement/reaction response is computed.

Carry the uncertainty box with the I/mu bound and retain the inherited residual Minkowski bound. Replace only this body contribution in the saved full Fenchel-gap upper; other body contributions, distributed-contact primal/dual bounds and laws remain unchanged.

Compare the new gap with the previous necessary threshold and recompute the unchanged unprojected lateral interval. A fixed-family ceiling at or above one is not an achieved exceedance, passing field or complete resistance. No projection is selected.

Physical stiffness/contact/restraint applicability, complete combined joint/member and cleat/fracture resistance remain open. Preserve current 100 bolts and 66 Hillman axes, rejected proposal history, panel/screw deferral, excluded actual fit and blank observations.
